title: Pregnancy Recipes: Iron-and-Folate Bowls You Can Cook in 30 Minutes
excerpt: Three tasty recipes pairing heme/non-heme iron with vitamin C — Vietnamese-inspired bowls with clear portions and food-safety notes.
content:
## Introduction
When pregnant, a woman's diet plays a crucial role in the development of her baby. Iron and folate are two essential nutrients for fetal development. Below are three simple and delicious recipes that combine iron with vitamin C, helping pregnant women supplement their bodies with enough nutrients.

## Recipe 1: Grilled Chicken Bowl with Steamed Broccoli and Lemon
* 100g grilled chicken (iron: 1.5mg)
* 100g steamed broccoli (vitamin C: 50mg)
* 1 lemon (vitamin C: 50mg)
* 1 cup cooked white rice (folate: 10mcg)

Grilled chicken is a rich source of heme iron, combined with steamed broccoli and lemon rich in vitamin C, which helps increase iron absorption. Pregnant women can grill chicken with a little olive oil and seasoning, then serve with steamed broccoli and lemon.

## Recipe 2: Beef Stir-Fry Bowl with Spinach and Bell Peppers
* 100g beef stir-fry (iron: 2mg)
* 100g spinach (vitamin C: 30mg)
* 1 bell pepper (vitamin C: 20mg)
* 1 cup cooked white rice (folate: 10mcg)

Beef stir-fry is a rich source of non-heme iron, combined with spinach and bell peppers rich in vitamin C, which helps increase iron absorption. Pregnant women can stir-fry beef with a little olive oil and seasoning, then serve with spinach and bell peppers.

## Recipe 3: Vegetarian Bowl with Tofu and Mixed Greens
* 100g tofu (iron: 1mg)
* 100g mixed greens (vitamin C: 20mg)
* 1 lemon (vitamin C: 50mg)
* 1 cup cooked white rice (folate: 10mcg)

Tofu is a rich source of non-heme iron, combined with mixed greens and lemon rich in vitamin C, which helps increase iron absorption. Pregnant women can cook tofu with a little olive oil and seasoning, then serve with mixed greens and lemon.

## Food Safety Notes
When cooking for pregnant women, it's essential to note food safety to avoid bacterial contamination and other health issues. Pregnant women should:
* Wash hands thoroughly before cooking
* Wash vegetables and fruits before cooking
* Cook meat and seafood thoroughly before serving
* Avoid eating raw or undercooked food

## Conclusion
The three recipes above are delicious and nutritious suggestions for pregnant women, helping supplement their bodies with enough iron and folate. Pregnant women should consult our [meal planner](/planner) for more recipe ideas and [prenatal nutrition category](/blog/prenatal-nutrition) for more information on pregnancy nutrition. Additionally, pregnant women should consult their healthcare provider before making any significant changes to their diet.

## When to Seek Care
If you are experiencing any symptoms such as severe fatigue, shortness of breath, or dizziness, seek medical care immediately. It is also essential to consult your healthcare provider before taking any supplements or making significant changes to your diet.

faqs.question: Why are iron and folate important for pregnant women?
faqs.answer: Iron and folate are essential nutrients for fetal development. Iron helps produce red blood cells, while folate helps prevent birth defects of the brain and spine.

faqs.question: How can I increase iron absorption?
faqs.answer: Pregnant women can increase iron absorption by combining iron with vitamin C, such as eating broccoli and lemon with meat or seafood.

faqs.question: What foods should I avoid during pregnancy?
faqs.answer: Pregnant women should avoid eating raw or undercooked food, as well as foods that may cause bacterial contamination, such as sushi or raw eggs.
